premises.text: Medication non-adherence is an extremely costly healthcare problem in deaths, costs, and lost revenues
premises.evidence_span: Medication adherence is arguably the most costly problem in health care today

premises.text: A patented smart pill bottle sends open/close timestamps and medication-amount data to the cloud for dosage comparison
premises.evidence_span: Every time the patient uses the bottle, it sends two pieces of data into the cloud

premises.text: On discrepancy the bottle uses lights and chimes plus phone or text alerts, and can ask why doses were missed to notify caregivers in real time
premises.evidence_span: we have on-bottle lights and chimes, and we also have phone or text message alerts as well

premises.text: Built-in cellular connectivity, long battery, normal-cap use, and no apps make the bottle easy and versatile for non-tech-savvy patients
premises.evidence_span: patients don't have to sync it to Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. It simply works the moment they get it from the pharmacy

premises.text: An open API integrates with healthcare partners and the bottle design supports labels and grip
premises.evidence_span: We've built this solution with an open API so we can easily integrate with all of our health care partners

premises.text: Specialty pharma companies pay for bottles that distribute high-cost drugs free to patients to raise adherence, refills, and pharma revenue
premises.evidence_span: partner with specialty pharma companies to distribute high-cost drugs in our bottle

value.text: Patients take the right pills at the right time with improved adherence and engagement
value.evidence_span: improve medication adherence and patient engagement

secondary_value.text: Pharma gains higher adherence, refills, and revenues
secondary_value.evidence_span: AdhereTech will increase adherence. refills, and ultimately revenues for the pharma company

causal_links.evidence_span: patients taking the right pill at the right time
if we notice a discrepancy, like the patient didn't take their pills, then we intervene
Patients will get this bottle from the specialty pharmacy completely free of charge

notes: Intervention modalities (lights/chimes/calls/texts/why-missed) folded as one intervention package (§4.1.7–8). Ease features (CDMA, battery, normal cap, alert channels) folded as one usability premise. Trials and named pharma partnerships treated as traction/evidence of the B2B model, not extra premises (§4.2). Team/board/GE excluded as biography. Patents folded into bottle mechanism (§4.1.1). Anti-template: problem, product, and pharma model separately revisable.
